overall_reason: Every region is the stock admin-dashboard kit (sidebar, four icon KPI cards with arrow deltas, smoothed line chart beside an unlabelled donut, recent-records table, upcoming list) filled with placeholder people and unsourced hospital figures; nothing belongs to a particular clinic or user.

findings.evidence: Four equal white cards, each an outline icon top-left, an arrow delta top-right and a big number over a grey label: 2,847 Total Patients / 94.2% Recovery Rate / 24 min Avg. Wait Time / 142 Beds Available. Failed T-DEFAULT-AGENT: 'healthcare analytics dashboard' yields exactly this row. Failed T-THREE-LINE: 'Recovery Rate 94.2%' is not falsifiable (recovered from what, over what period, for which cohort).
findings.after: Lead with the one number this user acts on today [DATA NEEDED: the clinician's or administrator's primary daily metric, its period and its definition]; move the rest into a compact labelled row with periods ('vs last week')
findings.why: The KPI wall is the most recognisable AI dashboard default (DVZ-106, DVZ-107); deltas with no period mean nothing.

findings.where: Recent Patients table and Upcoming Appointments list
findings.evidence: Patients "John Doe", "Sarah Miller", "Robert Johnson", "Emily Wilson" with emails at "@email.com"; appointments with "Michael Brown", "Lisa Anderson", "David Lee", "Jennifer Kim"; user "Dr. Roberts, Cardiologist". The sweep caught John Doe; the rest of the cast is the same default-name set. Failed T-FILLER: none of this data is real.
findings.after: [DATA NEEDED: realistic or anonymised sample records from the client], with varied name lengths and scripts to stress the table
findings.why: A default cast signals that no real records or users were considered; in a health product it also hides layout problems with real names and IDs.

findings.evidence: Donut of five colours (Cardiology, Neurology, Orthopedics, Pediatrics, Other) with no values, no totals and no unit: distribution of patients, admissions or beds is never said. Failed T-DELETION: removing it loses no fact the reader can read. Failed T-DIAGRAM-EARNS: a sorted bar or a 5-row table with counts teaches more.
findings.after: Sorted horizontal bars with counts and the measure in the title, e.g. 'Admissions this week by department' [DATA NEEDED: counts]
findings.why: Decorative donut beside a trend chart is the stock dashboard pairing.

findings.evidence: Admissions and Discharges drawn as heavily smoothed splines with a teal area fill under one series only; the curves overshoot between daily points (Thu peak bulges above the 65 point), inventing values for counts that are integers per day.
findings.after: Straight segments or daily bars for counts (DVZ-110), no area fill, direct labels at line ends instead of a bottom legend
findings.why: Chart.js defaults (smooth tension, fill, dot markers, bottom legend) were accepted rather than chosen for the data.

findings.evidence: h2 "Healthcare Analytics" with sub "Overview of patient data and hospital metrics"; section heads "Recent Patients", "Upcoming Appointments", "Department Distribution". Failed T-RIVAL-NAME: every line stays true for any hospital dashboard. Failed T-FIVE-SECOND: for whom (which ward, which role) and what to do are unanswered.
findings.before: "Overview of patient data and hospital metrics"
findings.after: State the scope and moment: '[DATA NEEDED: ward/clinic name], today, [date]' and put the one action (e.g. next appointment, patients awaiting review) first
findings.why: Category-label headings and a restating subline are filler; they name the page type, not its content.

findings.evidence: "Checkup - Michael Brown", "Surgery - Lisa Anderson", "Consultation - David Lee", "Lab Results - Jennifer Kim": TYPE - Name labels repeated on four identical grey cards, each with the time right-aligned and a grey description below. The sweep caught the dash labels; the judgment is that the card list duplicates what a time-sorted agenda row would show.
findings.before: card: "Checkup - Michael Brown" / 9:00 AM / General Health Examination
findings.after: Agenda rows: '09:00  Michael Brown  Checkup, general examination', time first in tabular figures, no card per row
findings.why: One card per list item is the card-kit habit (SLP-005, SLP-155).

findings.evidence: Inter for all text plus a monospace face (font-mono, intended Fira Code; renders as a Courier-like fallback in capture) for the big KPI numbers and '#PT-2847', which wraps onto two lines in the ID column. Mono is used as 'data costume' rather than for alignment.
findings.after: Use the body face with font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums for figures; keep mono only if IDs are copied by staff, and stop '#PT-2847' wrapping (white-space: nowrap)
findings.why: Mono-as-costume (SLP-192) on stat figures is a dashboard default.

strengths: Information architecture is plausible for a clinic: appointments with times and procedure names are concrete in kind, even if the data is placeholder.
not_investigated: Tailwind was shimmed (manifest: tailwind.config ignored), so custom 'primary' and status-pill colours, the active 'Weekly' tab fill and avatar circle fills are missing from the render; colour choices were not judged
Fonts Fira Sans / Fira Code were shimmed; typeface judgment limited to roles
